Directions. Identify the segment of the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

As long as Stefan is/ (A) the head of the project,/ (B) he will not be allowing any changes/ (C) in the rules. (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e., ‘he will not be allowing any changes’- the error lies in this part only.

  • This is a conditional sentence, and in this type of sentence, one sentence depends upon the other because of cause and effect.
  • In this case, this type of sentence follows a special structure.
  • Conditional words are If, even if, until, unless, as soon as, when, while, as long as, after, etc.
  1. Conditional word + subject + v1/v5 + object, subject + will/ shall/ may + v1 + object.
  2. If + subject + v2 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + v1 + object.
  3. If + subject + had + v3 + object, subject + would/ should/ could/ might + have + v3 + object.
  4. Had + subject + v3 + object, subject + would + have + v3 + object.
  • The given sentence follows rule number ‘1’, and according to the rule, the error lies in Part ‘C’.

For example- As long as there is petrol in the car, we will continue driving.

  • In the given sentence, ‘will not be allowing’ is wrongly used instead of ‘will not allow’ in the main clause.

Hence, ‘will not be allowing’ should be replaced by ‘will not allow’.

So, the correct sentence is:

“As long as Stefan is the head of the project, he will not allow any changes in the rules.” 

The conditional expressions, for example- ‘as long as’, ‘so long as’, ‘on condition that’ is used to impose certain conditions or set restrictions to circumstances.

questions.text: Choose the synonym of the word 'Incriminating'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Implicating.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Incriminating' means To make someone appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.
    • Example: They were afraid of answering the questions and incriminating themselves.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Absolving - To declare someone free from guilt, obligation, or punishment.
      • Example: He showed his desire for peace by absolving the king.
    • Exculpating - To show or declare that someone is not guilty of wrongdoing.
      • Example: I want him to appreciate that my words were not intended for the purpose of exculpating anybody.
    • Vindicating - To clear someone of blame or suspicion.
      • Example: New evidence emerged, vindicating him completely.
    • Exonerating - To absolve someone from blame for a fault or wrongdoing.
      • Example: I certainly have no intent of exonerating anybody.
    • Implicating - To show someone to be involved in a crime.
      • Example: He was in the public dock, confessing everything, implicating everybody.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 5.

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word 'Incriminating' are "Implicating, Blaming, Accusing".
  • The antonyms of the word 'Incriminating' are "Absolving, Exculpating, Vindicating".

questions.text: Choose the antonym of the word 'Suspicion'.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Certitude.'

Key Points

  • The word 'Suspicion' means The act or an instance of suspecting something wrong without proof or on slight evidence.
    • Example: I had a suspicion that he was there.
  • Let's look at the meaning of the given options:-
    • Certitude​ - Absolute certainty or conviction that something is the case.
      • Example: We have this definite certitude that he will be freed.
    • Surmise - A supposition that something may be true, even though there is no evidence to confirm it.
      • Example: Her surmise turned out to be right.
    • Conjecture - An opinion or conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information.
      • Example: The judge dismissed the evidence as pure conjecture.
    • Speculation - The forming of a theory or conjecture without firm evidence.
      • Example: The minister dismissed the newspaper reports as pure speculation.
    • Hunch - A feeling or guess based on intuition rather than fact.
      • Example: I had a hunch that Vikas and I would work well together.
         

Hence, the only possible answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • The antonyms of the word 'Suspicion' are "Certitude, Assurance, Certainty".
  • The synonyms of the word 'Suspicion' are "Surmise, Conjecture, Speculation".

questions.text:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is underlined. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part, which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the option that indicates ‘No improvement’.

Although he is able to make political enemies with this decision, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, does not mind doing it for the sake of public welfare.

  1. Although he is liable to make
  2. Although he is accountable for making
  3. Although he is liable from making
questions.explanation:
The adjective ‘able’ means ‘to have skills to do something’, whereas 'liable' means 'at risk of or subject to experiencing or suffering something unpleasant’. Therefore, instead of ‘able’, ‘liable’ should be used.

‘liable’ is followed by preposition ‘to’ or ‘for’.

For example-

  • If you don’t take care of yourself, you’re liable to get sick.
  • He is still liable for repaying his student loan.

‘accountable’ is synonymous to ‘liable’, thus can be used. It is followed by preposition ‘to’ or ‘for’. ‘accountable to’ is used when accountability is towards ‘someone’ and ‘accountable for’ is used when accountability is towards ‘something’.

Thus, alternatives A and B are grammatically correct.

Below a word is given followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence/s which best expresses the meaning of the word. Choose Option 5 (None of these) if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

MENDACIOUS

A) As a politician, he was very adept at speaking mendaciously in public.
B) Dogged and ingenious interrogation of a mendacious suspect finally reveals the truth.
C) The form of government was borrowed largely from those prevailing in the mendacious orders.

options.text: Both A and C are correct
Both A and B are correct
Both B and C are correct

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Both A and B are correct

Key Points

  • Sentence A) As a politician, he was very adept at speaking mendaciously in public.
    • Here mendaciously is correctly used. 'Mendacious' means given to or characterized by deception or falsehood or divergence from absolute truth. Thus the sentence means that as a politician, he was expert in speaking lies in public.
  • Sentence B) Dogged and ingenious interrogation of a mendacious suspect finally gets at the truth.
    • Here mendacious is correctly used. 'Mendacious' means given to or characterized by deception or falsehood or divergence from absolute truth. 
  • Sentence C) The form of government was borrowed largely from those prevailing in the mendacious orders.
    • Here the use of mendacious makes no sense. 'Mendicant' should be there in place of 'Mendacious'. Mendicant here means of, relating to, belonging to, or constituting a religious order combining monastic life and outside religious activity and originally owning neither personal nor community property.

So sentence A and B are correct.

Ambivalent here is correctly used. 'Ambivalent' means having mixed feelings.

11) The person like KXIP and DC are in separate circles.

12) R does not like MI.  (From here Case 2 eliminated)

Here, A, B, C and D sit in the inner circle while S sits in the outer circle.

Hence, S does not belong to the group.

Step 2: The second element of each code represent the number of consonants in the word.

Step 3. The third element of each code represents the second letter of the word from the right end.

Their agreement was to donate 40% of cumulative profits, and split the remainder in their investment ratios. Investment of Mantu and Kisor Rs. (7x + 8000) & Rs. (3.5x + 4000) respectively. 

Donated 40% of their total profits

Profit = Investment × Time

If the time of investment is equal then the ratio of investment = ratio of profit

Calculation:

∵ Ratio of profits = Ratio of investment

⇒ 1 unit = 12000

Which is the 60% of the total profit.

Total profit = 36000/60% × 100

Total profit = 60000

Hence, the correct answer is 60000.

questions.text: Which indexing technique is best suited for high-cardinality columns in a data warehouse fact table?

options.text: Bitmap index, for efficient compression of unique values
Cluster index, for physical row ordering
Hash index, for exact equality matches only
B-tree index, for fast range scans on many distinct values

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B-tree index

Key Points

  • B-tree indexes are best suited for high-cardinality columns in a data warehouse fact table.
  • High-cardinality columns are those with many distinct values, such as unique IDs or timestamps.
  • B-tree indexes provide efficient access to data for both exact matches and range scans.
  • They are particularly effective for querying large datasets with many distinct values, as they allow fast lookups and sorting.
  • Unlike bitmap indexes, which are ideal for low-cardinality columns, B-tree indexes can handle diverse and numerous unique values efficiently.

Additional Information

  • Bitmap Index: Bitmap indexes are useful for low-cardinality columns where the number of distinct values is small. They are not suitable for high-cardinality columns as the index size becomes large and inefficient.
  • Cluster Index: Cluster indexes physically order rows in a table based on the index key. While they are useful for certain scenarios, they are not specifically designed for handling high-cardinality columns efficiently.
  • Hash Index: Hash indexes work well for exact equality searches but do not support range queries, making them less effective for high-cardinality columns requiring range scans.
  • Full-text Index: Full-text indexes are specialized for searching text-based data and are not suitable for handling high-cardinality columns in a fact table.

questions.text: What is the key benefit of using a Kimball methodology in data warehouse design?

options.text: It emphasizes a normalized, entity-relationship model first
It focuses on dimensional modeling for business-driven, agile development
It prioritizes real-time data integration over batch loads
It avoids ETL by direct source querying
It centralizes all metadata in operational systems

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is It focuses on dimensional modeling for business-driven, agile development.

Key Points

  • Kimball methodology prioritizes dimensional modeling, which organizes data into facts and dimensions. This approach makes data intuitive and easy to query for business users.
  • It is designed to support agile development, enabling iterative design and rapid delivery of business insights.
  • Unlike normalized models, Kimball's dimensional modeling is optimized for performance and usability, especially in data warehouses.
  • This methodology emphasizes aligning the data warehouse design with specific business needs, ensuring that it addresses key business questions effectively.
  • Its focus on business-driven development ensures that the warehouse remains relevant and valuable to end users.

Additional Information

  • Option 1: Emphasizing a normalized, entity-relationship model is a characteristic of the Inmon methodology, not Kimball. Inmon focuses on a top-down approach with a highly normalized structure.
  • Option 3: Prioritizing real-time data integration is not the primary focus of Kimball. While real-time integration can be implemented, the methodology mainly emphasizes batch processing for analytical purposes.
  • Option 4: Kimball does not avoid ETL (Extract, Transform, Load). In fact, it heavily relies on ETL processes to load data into dimensional models.
  • Option 5: Centralizing metadata in operational systems is not a feature of Kimball. It focuses on creating a data warehouse tailored to end-user needs, not operational metadata centralization.

questions.text: ________ CSMA protocol, after the station finds the line idle, it sends or refrains from sending based on the outcome of a random number generator.
questions.explanation:
Key Points

 In p-persistent CSMA protocol, after the station finds the line idle, it sends or refrains from sending based on the outcome of a random number generator.

P-persistent: 
In p-persistent CSMA, when a transmitting station has a frame to send and it senses a busy channel, it waits for the end of the transmission, and then transmits with a probability p. Since, it sends with a probability p, the name p – persistent CSMA is given.

1-persistent: 

n 1-persistent CSMA, the station continuously senses the channel to check its state i.e. idle or busy so that it can transfer data or not. In case when the channel is busy, the station will wait for the channel to become idle. Due to probability 1, it is called 1-persistent CSMA.

Non-persistent: 
Non-persistent CSMA is a non-aggressive transmission algorithm. When the transmitting node is ready to transmit data, it senses the transmission medium for idle or busy. If idle, then it transmits immediately. When the transmitting node is ready to transmit data, it senses the transmission medium for idle or busy.
0-persistent:  

Each node is given a transmission order by a supervisory node. When the transmission channel is idle, nodes wait for their time slot in accordance with their assigned transmission sequence. The node that is given the task of broadcasting first does so immediately. 

Hence the correct answer is p-persistent.

questions.text: Which clause is evaluated after aggregation but before final sorting?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is HAVING(Option 3).

Key Points

  • HAVING clause is used in SQL queries to filter results after aggregation functions are applied.
  • It acts as a post-aggregation filter, unlike the WHERE clause, which applies filters before aggregation.
  • The HAVING clause is typically used with GROUP BY to specify filtering conditions for grouped data.
  • For example, to filter groups where the aggregate condition is met, HAVING is essential.
  • It allows conditions to be applied to aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, AVG, MAX, MIN.
  • ORDER BY is used after HAVING for final sorting of results.

Additional Information

  • WHERE Clause:
    • Filters rows before aggregation is applied.
    • Cannot use aggregate functions like COUNT or SUM directly.
  • ORDER BY Clause:
    • Used to sort the final query result in ascending or descending order.
    • Placed at the end of the SQL query.
  • GROUP BY Clause:
    • Used to group rows that have the same values in specified columns.
    • Often used with aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM, etc.

questions.text: ________ constraints ensure that a value that appears in one relation for a given set of attributes also appears for a certain set of attributes in another relation.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Concept:

Referential Integrity constraints ensure that a value that appears in one relation for a given set of attributes also appears for a certain set of attributes in another relation.

A referential integrity constraint is also known as a foreign key constraint. A foreign key is a key whose values are derived from the Primary key of another table.

The table from which the values are derived is known as the Master or Referenced Table, and the table into which the values are inserted is known as the Child or Referencing Table. In other words, the table containing the foreign key is referred to as the child table, and the table containing the primary key/candidate key is referred to as the referenced or parent table. The candidate key in the database relational model can be defined as a set of attributes with zero or more attributes.

The syntax of the Master Table or Referenced table is:

CREATE TABLE Student (Roll int PRIMARY KEY, Name varchar(25), Course varchar(10) );

Here  Roll is acting as the Primary Key, which will help in deriving the value of foreign key in the child table.

The syntax of Child Table or Referencing table is:

CREATE TABLE Subject (Roll int references Student, SubCode int, SubName varchar(10) );

Roll is acting as Foreign Key, whose values are derived using the Roll value of Primary key from Master table.

Hence the correct answer is Referential Integrity.

questions.text: For a metadata repository in a multi-source data warehouse tracking derivatives contracts, which conceptual role does it play in facilitating impact analysis when a source schema changes?

options.text: It documents lineage and dependencies to trace change effects
It optimizes physical storage layouts dynamically
It performs automatic data cleansing on metadata
It generates ETL code without user input
It stores raw data extracts for direct querying

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 1: It documents lineage and dependencies to trace change effects.

Key Points

  • The primary role of a metadata repository in a multi-source data warehouse is to act as a centralized storage location for metadata.
  • It documents the lineage of data, showing the origin, flow, and transformations of data across the system.
  • When a source schema changes, the metadata repository helps trace the impact of this change on downstream systems, reports, and analyses.
  • Dependencies between data sources, ETL processes, and reports are tracked, making it easier to assess and manage the consequences of schema modifications.
  • This functionality is critical for ensuring data integrity and minimizing disruptions in a complex multi-source environment.

Additional Information

  • Option 2: Optimizing physical storage layouts dynamically is not the role of a metadata repository. This is typically handled by the database management system (DBMS).
  • Option 3: Performing automatic data cleansing on metadata is outside the scope of a metadata repository, which focuses on storing and managing metadata, not altering it.
  • Option 4: While metadata can assist in generating ETL code, the process usually requires user input and oversight. Metadata repositories do not generate ETL code autonomously.
  • Option 5: Storing raw data extracts for direct querying is the responsibility of a data lake or data warehouse, not a metadata repository.
